mechanism_narrative: The continuing rebound in WORKPLACES mobility raises weekday foot traffic and adjacent retail errands, so RETAIL_REC will keep improving over the next four weeks as commuting normalizes.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -17.0 to -11.3 while RETAIL_REC improved from -22.4 to -13.3 over the snapshot window
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES stops rising or turns down and RETAIL_REC remains below its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT recovers from below -30% toward the mid -20s, access to shopping districts improves and RETAIL_REC follows within two weeks; the observed transit rebound should therefore push retail higher next.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -28% after being below -30% for at least one week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -37.1 to -26.6 across the snapshot while RETAIL_REC also rose
failure_condition: If TRANSIT exceeds -28% but RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days, or RETAIL_REC falls despite transit recovery, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Higher RESIDENTIAL mobility reflects more time spent near home, which reduces discretionary retail trips and keeps RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed elevated at 9.0 to 5.1 while RETAIL_REC remained negative
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays elevated but RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A joint rise in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS signals more neighborhood out-of-home activity and errand chaining, which spills over into retail visits and lifts RETAIL_REC within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed above 9% and PARKS turned positive while RETAIL_REC improved
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS are both positive but RETAIL_REC does not increase within 7 days, or if one proxy rises while the other falls and retail still drops, the interaction claim fails.

mechanism_narrative: If mobility restrictions are easing, the combination of rising WORKPLACES and TRANSIT acts as a reopening signal that expands discretionary shopping; RETAIL_REC should trend upward over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improved steadily across the snapshot
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise for two weeks but RETAIL_REC is flat or lower over the following 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-holiday normalization window, higher PARKS usage diverts discretionary time toward outdoor leisure rather than malls, causing RETAIL_REC to weaken over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains above 0% for two straight weeks after a negative week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -14.4 to 5.6 while RETAIL_REC remained negative
failure_condition: If PARKS stays positive but RETAIL_REC improves over the next 14 days instead of weakening, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous decline in RESIDENTIAL and rise in WORKPLACES indicates a shift back to out-of-home routines, and that shift should continue to push RETAIL_REC above its recent average over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls while WORKPLACES rises for at least two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 9.0 to 5.1 while WORKPLACES improved from -17.0 to -11.3
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL falls and WORKPLACES rises but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior 4-week mean within 28 days, the mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT remains deeply depressed even as WORKPLACES improve, commuting substitution is incomplete and retail demand lags; RETAIL_REC therefore stays below the last-month level over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -25% while WORKPLACES rises
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was still -26.6 at the decision time despite a WORKPLACES recovery
failure_condition: If TRANSIT stays below -25% and WORKPLACES rises, but RETAIL_REC increases above its last-4-week mean within 28 days, the hypothesis fails.
